## R Markdown

This is an R Markdown document. Markdown is a simple formatting syntax for authoring HTML, PDF, and MS Word documents. For more details on using R Markdown see <http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com>.

When you click the **Knit** button a document will be generated that includes both content as well as the output of any embedded R code chunks within the document. You can embed an R code chunk like this:


## Including Plots

You can also embed plots, for example:

```{r pressure, echo=FALSE}
plot(pressure)
```

Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.


```{r}
# abbreviated sf example, intention is to demonstrate merging w/ other data
# and simple chloropleth mapping

install.packages("viridis")
library(sf)
library(data.table)
library(viridis) # for nice colors
```
```{r}
# sf comes with some example data, including a North Carolina
# county shapefile.
nc <- st_read(system.file("shape/nc.shp", package="sf"))
class(nc)
names(nc)
```
```{r}
# calculate a new numeric variable: perim:area ratio
nc$PAratio <- nc$PERIMETER / nc$AREA
hist(nc$PAratio)
```

```{r}
# let's make a plot of NC counties
plot(nc[1])
# only pulls out the column without the geometry - loses it spatial information
plot(nc$AREA)
```
```{r}
# now colored by P:A
plot(nc[16])
```
```{r}
# finer control of colors
?sf::plot
```

```{r}
# from classIntervals package
# GIS functionality for defining color breaks 
# style: "fixed", "sd", "equal", "pretty", "quantile", "kmeans", "hclust", "bclust", "fisher", "jenks", "dpih", "headtails", or "maximum"
plot(nc[16], breaks="fisher")
plot(nc["PAratio"], breaks="kmeans", pal=colorRampPalette(magma(10)), border="white", key.pos=4, axes=T)
```
```{r}
#####################
# Lets practice merging sf objects with some other data source

# simple example w/ fake data.table, here we join a new data.table
# with the nc sf object based on county FIPS code. The new data.table
# contains a plotting color and random numeric value for 20 random
# counties.
unique_FIPS <- unique(nc$FIPS)
# sample 20 of the FIPS code without replacement - random sampling 
DF <- data.table(FIPS=sample(unique_FIPS, 20), plotcol=sample(viridis(20)), NewValue=rnorm(20))
nc <- merge(nc, DF, by="FIPS", all.x=TRUE)
# only the 20 columns that select have the colorised column full - the 20 we selected 
plot(nc[,1], col=nc$plotcol)
nc[is.na(nc$plotcol), ]$plotcol <- "grey"
plot(nc[,1], col=nc$plotcol)
nc[!is.na(nc$NewValue), c("NAME", "plotcol")]
```

```{r}
#############################
# And now with some actual data
# load some NASS data about NC tobacco production in 2017
# It originally fails to upload because there is no way to define the columns
tobacco <- read.table("~/Downloads/NC_tobacco_2017.csv")
?read.table
```


```{r}
# ok, let's define the separator, strip white space, make sure it knows there's a header, and take care of quoting
tobacco <- read.table("~/Data/NC_tobacco_2017.csv", sep=",", quote="\"", strip.white=TRUE, head=T)
names(tobacco)
tobacco[1,]
```
```{r}
# is there an easier way?
tobacco <- fread("~/Data/NC_tobacco_2017.csv")
tobacco[1,]
names(tobacco)
?fread
tobacco <- fread("~/Data/NC_tobacco_2017.csv", check.names=T)
names(tobacco)
```

```{r}
# What's in these data?
# This is very important for HW 1 
tobacco[, lapply(.SD, unique), .SDcols=c("Year", "State", "Geo.Level", "Ag.District")]
tobacco[, unique(Commodity)]
# the data is not tidy - it is in long form - read the line below 
tobacco[, unique(Data.Item)]
tobacco[, unique(Domain)]
tobacco[, .N, by=.(Data.Item, Domain)]
# Pulling out one unique tobacco item 
tobacco[Data.Item == "TOBACCO - PRODUCTION, MEASURED IN LB"]
# verify this gets us down to ONE VALUE PER COUNTY!
# run this first on your hw to make sure that you are getting one record for one item for one county for one year 
tobacco[Data.Item == "TOBACCO - PRODUCTION, MEASURED IN LB", .N, by="County"][, max(N)]
# now subset to a smaller table
tobacco <- subset(tobacco, Data.Item == "TOBACCO - PRODUCTION, MEASURED IN LB")
```

```{r}
# we have an issue with the Value column
tobacco[1:25, Value]
as.numeric(tobacco[1:25, Value])
```

```{r}
as.numeric(tobacco[1:25, gsub(",", "", Value)]) # this is what we want
tobacco[, Value := as.numeric(gsub(",", "", Value))] # so we calculate in place over all the data
tobacco[1:25, Value]
hist(tobacco[, Value])
```
```{r}
# let's merge w/ the NC county and map production
# first, we need a merging column
names(nc)
# looking at what the FIPs code is
nc$FIPS[1:10]
# looking for a join key in the tobacco dataset
names(tobacco)
# the fips code is located in two different columns 
tobacco[1:10, .(State.ANSI, County.ANSI)]
# paste them together to make a new column called "FIPS" in tobacco
tobacco[, FIPS := paste(State.ANSI, formatC(County.ANSI, width="3", flag="0"), sep="")]
```


```{r}
# let's plot by tobacco production
# nc needs to be first so that the joined dataset with be a spatial dataset
nc <- merge(nc, tobacco, by="FIPS", all.x=T)
plot(nc["Value"])
plot(nc["Value"], breaks="jenks", key.pos=4, axes=T, main="Tobacco Production 2017 (lb)")
```
